;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Kabul gurdwara attack]]
**A bomb explodes near a Sikh [[crematorium]] in [[Kabul]], wounding a child and disrupting funerals for 25 people bombed and shot the day prior. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/child-injured-in-blast-near-sikh-crematorium-in-afghan-capital/articleshow/74832361.cms (''Times of India'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mali]]an opposition leader [[Soumaïla Cissé]] and six others are taken [[hostage]] by [[jihadist]]s in the northern [[Tombouctou Region]]. Cissé's bodyguard was killed and two others injured in the [[ambush]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mali-security/mali-opposition-leader-taken-hostage-with-six-others-party-idUSKBN21D1DA (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The death toll from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in the U.S. reaches 1,200. The total number of cases in the country is 83,097. The U.S. has surpassed [[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China|China in number]] of active cases, making it the country with the most cases in the world. [https://www.worldometers.info/coronavirus/#countries (Worldometer)]
****[[U.S. state and local government response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colorado]]
******[[Governor of Colorado|Colorado Governor]] [[Jared Polis]] issues a [[stay-at-home order]] until April 11. [https://chicago.suntimes.com/coronavirus/2020/3/26/21195448/colorados-stay-at-home-coronavirus-covid-19-jared-polis-flatten-the-curve (''Chicago Suntimes'')]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire]]
******[[Governor of New Hampshire|New Hampshire Governor]] [[Chris Sununu]] issues a [[stay-at-home order]] until May 4. [https://www.wmur.com/article/live-at-3-sununu-gives-update-on-covid-19/31941704# (WMUR)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania#Samoa|COVID-19 pandemic in Samoa]]
****[[Samoa]] begins a national lockdown announced by the [[Prime Minister of Samoa|Prime Minister]]. Those who do not comply with the lockdown's requirements will be fined. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/412647/samoa-officially-on-lock-down (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****The [[Congress of Deputies]] approves extending the Alarm Status until 12 April. [https://elpais.com/espana/2020-03-24/un-congreso-vacio-para-ratificar-con-reproches-la-prorroga-del-estado-de-alarma.html (''El País'')]
****[[Spain]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Spain)|Ministry of Health]] reports 655 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the country's death toll to over 4,000. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-spain-emergency/spain-extends-coronavirus-lockdown-in-war-to-buy-medical-supplies-idUKKBN21D0R7?il=0 (Reuters)]
****[[Real Madrid CF]]'s [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]] is to be used to store medical materials. [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/mar/26/real-madrid-stadium-to-be-used-in-fight-against-coronavirus-santiago-bernabeu (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Department of Health and Social Care]] reports 103 more deaths from COVID-19, the highest daily death toll in the country to date, bringing the death toll in the [[United Kingdom]] to 578 and 11,658 confirmed cases. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-52056534 (BBC News)]
****An 84-year-old inmate at [[HMP Littlehey]] in [[Cambridgeshire]] has become the first UK prisoner to die from COVID-19, according to the [[Ministry of Justice (United Kingdom)|Ministry of Justice]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/26/first-prisoner-in-uk-dies-from-coronavirus (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****The [[Republic of Ireland]] reports 255 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 and 10 more deaths, doubling the country's death toll to 19. The median age of the 19 patients who have died is 79 years old. [https://metro.co.uk/2020/03/26/irelands-coronavirus-death-toll-doubles-10-people-die-12463279/?ito=cbshare (''Metro'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports 365 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the country's total to 1,696. French health authorities say 3,375 people with the virus remain in serious condition requiring life support. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200326-france-reports-new-spike-of-365-daily-coronavirus-deaths (France 24)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Armenia]]
****Ministry of Health confirms the first death in the country from COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-armenia/corrected-armenia-reports-first-death-related-to-coronavirus-idUSR4N2B506B (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China]] announces that travel will be suspended to the country as imported cases increase. [https://www.newsweek.com/china-suspend-entry-foreigners-coronavirus-continues-spread-abroad-1494493 (''Newsweek'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] is expected to impose night curfew to tackle COVID-19 as the country begins a nationwide disinfection campaign. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/coronavirus-uae-imposes-overnight-curfew-disinfection-campaign (''Middle East Eye'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Afghanistan]]
****[[Afghanistan]] is to release 10,000 prisoners over the age of 55 in response to the coronavirus pandemic. Those released will not include members of the [[Taliban]] and [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-afghanistan-prison/afghanistan-to-release-10000-prisoners-to-slow-spread-of-coronavirus-idUKKBN21D32E (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nicaragua]]
****[[Nicaragua]] reports the country's first death from COVID-19, a patient with [[HIV/AIDS]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-nicaragua/nicaragua-reports-first-death-from-coronavirus-idUKKBN21E043?il=0 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
****[[Venezuela]]n Vice President [[Delcy Rodríguez]] reports the country's first death from COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-venezuela-death/venezuela-confirms-first-coronavirus-death-official-idUSKBN21D3Q3 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ethiopia]]
****[[President of Ethiopia|Ethiopian President]] [[Sahle-Work Zewde]] pardons more than 4,000 prisoners in an attempt to prevent coronavirus spread. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/03/26/africa/ethiopia-pardons-4000-prisoners-over-coronavirus/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[Iran–United States relations]], [[Iraq–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Treasury Secretary]] imposes fresh [[United States sanctions against Iran|sanctions]] on Iran, blacklisting 20 Iran- and Iraq-linked companies and individuals. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-iran-sanctions/u-s-imposes-fresh-sanctions-on-iranian-individuals-companies-treasury-idUSKBN21D2B8 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 G20 Riyadh summit]]
**World leaders [[2020 extraordinary G20 summit on COVID-19|convene]] virtually to coordinate a response to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory/world-leaders-meet-virtually-coordinate-virus-response-69806671 (ABC News)]
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice|United States Justice Department]] announces charges against [[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] for [[drug trafficking]], offering up to a [[$]]15 million award for his arrest. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nicolas-maduro-venezuela-president-department-justice-charges/ (CBS News)] [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-usa-venezuela-maduro-rewards/u-s-announces-reward-up-to-15-million-for-venezuelas-maduro-idUKKBN21D2LS?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Christchurch mosque shootings]]
**Brenton Tarrant pleads guilty to [[murder]]ing 51 people and [[attempting to murder]] 40 as well as a [[terrorism in New Zealand|terrorism]] charge in relation to two [[mass shooting]]s in [[Christchurch]], [[New Zealand]], on 15 March 2019. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-52044013 (BBC News)]
*A [[Texas]] man is arrested for making death threats to [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] and other [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] on [[Facebook]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/26/us/texas-man-pelosi-death-threats-virus.html (''New York Times'')]

;Science and technology
*The [[United States Space Force]] launches its first satellite into space aboard an [[Atlas V]] rocket. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/us-space-force-launches-billion-dollar-military-communications-satellite/ (CBS News)] 

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[2020 WNBA draft]]
***The [[WNBA draft]] will go as planned on April 17, but will be a virtual event due to the coronavirus. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-basketball-wnba-draft-april17-coronav-idUSKBN21D2PR (Reuters)]
**The [[2020 Indianapolis 500]] will be delayed until August 23, marking the first time in history that the event will not be held in May. [https://www.indystar.com/story/news/history/retroindy/2020/03/26/indy-500-delayed-6-times-race-didnt-run/2916786001/ (''Indianapolis Star'')]
**The [[Candidates Tournament 2020]] is suspended after seven of 14 matches, following Russia's closure of international air traffic. [https://chess24.com/en/read/news/fide-candidates-tournament-stopped-at-halfway (chess24.com)]
